status: FROZEN - do not edit. Record any disputed judgement as a separate sensitivity analysis file.

provenance.built_from: data/processed/pages.json (text extracted from the four source PDFs) and data/processed/recommendations.json
provenance.method: Each query was answered by reading the guideline text page by page and pre-registering the passages that genuinely contain the answer. Passages were chosen BEFORE any retrieval run and WITHOUT looking at retriever output.
provenance.independence: Relevance is anchored to document_id + page range + required clinical facts. It never references chunk_id, chunk ordering, similarity score, or retriever behaviour, so it stays valid across re-chunking.
provenance.note: This is a FRESH evaluation baseline for the current repository. It is NOT a continuation of, and is NOT numerically comparable to, any previous audit.

relevance_rule.description: A retrieved chunk counts as RELEVANT to a query if and only if BOTH conditions hold.
relevance_rule.condition_1_provenance: chunk.document_id equals answer_passage.document_id AND the chunk page span [page_start, page_end] overlaps the passage page span [page_start, page_end]. Overlap test: chunk.page_start <= passage.page_end AND chunk.page_end >= passage.page_start.
relevance_rule.condition_2_facts: The normalised chunk text satisfies at least `min_groups` of the query's required_facts groups. A group is satisfied if ANY of its regex alternatives matches.
relevance_rule.multiple_passages: A query may have several acceptable answer passages; matching any one of them satisfies condition 1. No specific chunk_id is ever required.
text_normalisation: map the en-dash/minus/'>=' glyph variants used by ESVS to ASCII space
collapse all runs of whitespace to a single space
relevance_rule.regex_flags: re.IGNORECASE, applied to the normalised text

metrics.P@k: (number of relevant chunks in the top-k) / k
metrics.MRR: 1 / (rank of the first relevant chunk within the top-10); 0 if none in the top-10
metrics.Recall@k: (number of distinct pre-registered answer passages covered by at least one relevant chunk in the top-k) / (total answer passages for that query). Passage-level, NOT chunk-level, so it is stable across re-chunking.
metrics.Relevant Top-1: count of queries whose rank-1 chunk is relevant
metrics.Answering@5: true if at least one relevant chunk appears in the top-5
metrics.aggregation: unweighted mean over the 10 queries (counts for Relevant Top-1)
metrics.retrieval_depth: top-10 retrieved for every query; deeper metrics are computed from the same single ranked list
metrics.tie_breaking: the retriever's own deterministic ordering is used as-is; no re-sorting is applied by the evaluator

queries.query: What are the recommendations for screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm?

answer_passages.why: States the 1-time ultrasonography screening recommendation for men 65-75 who have ever smoked, plus the selective-offer and against-routine statements.
Repeats the graded screening recommendations with the population and net-benefit assessment.
Recommendation 11: ultrasound screening for early detection of AAA in high risk populations to reduce death from rupture (Class I, Level A).
NHS AAA screening programme recommendations: inform men aged 66 or over, encourage self-referral with risk factors, consider ultrasound for women 70+.
One-time ultrasound screening in men or women 65 to 75 years of age with a history of tobacco use (1/A), plus first-degree relatives and >75 years.

queries.query: What AAA diameter is generally associated with consideration of elective repair?

answer_passages.section_ref: 4.4 Diameter threshold for elective repair - Recommendations 20-23
answer_passages.why: Rec 20: men <55 mm not recommended for elective repair. Rec 22: men >=55 mm should be considered. Rec 21/23: women <50 mm not recommended, >=50 mm may be considered.
Elective repair for a fusiform AAA >= 5.5 cm (1/A); repair in women with AAA 5.0-5.4 cm (2/B).
Consider repair if asymptomatic and 5.5 cm or larger, or >4.0 cm with growth >1 cm in 1 year, or symptomatic.

queries.query: What surveillance strategy is recommended for small abdominal aortic aneurysms?

answer_passages.why: RESCAN-based intervals: every 5 years for 25-29 mm, 3 years for 30-39 mm, annually for 40-49 mm, every 6 months for 50-54 mm; separate sex-specific recommendation for women.
Surveillance imaging at 3-year intervals for 3.0-3.9 cm, 12-month for 4.0-4.9 cm, 6-month for 5.0-5.4 cm; rescreen after 10 years if <3 cm.
Offer surveillance with aortic ultrasound to people with an asymptomatic AAA, using the NHS AAA screening programme frequency.

queries.query: What are the indications for endovascular aneurysm repair?

answer_passages.why: Rec 65: for most patients with suitable anatomy and reasonable life expectancy, endovascular repair should be considered the preferred elective modality.
For patients with a ruptured AAA and suitable anatomy, endovascular repair is recommended as the first line treatment option.
Consider EVAR for unruptured AAA with abdominal copathology (hostile abdomen, horseshoe kidney, stoma), or where anaesthetic risk/comorbidity contraindicates open surgical repair.
Consider EVAR or open surgical repair for ruptured AAA; open repair if standard EVAR unsuitable.
If anatomically feasible, EVAR is recommended over open repair for a ruptured AAA (1/C).

queries.query: What are the risk factors associated with abdominal aortic aneurysm?

answer_passages.why: Important risk factors for AAA include older age, male sex, smoking, first-degree relative with AAA; other factors include CAD, cerebrovascular disease, atherosclerosis, hypercholesterolaemia, hypertension.
Smoking is the strongest risk factor (OR >3); other risk factors include atherosclerosis, hypertension, ethnicity, and family history.
The dominant risk factor for AAA, apart from male sex and age, is smoking; ~75% of AAA cases attributable to smoking.
Enumerated risk factors: COPD, coronary/cerebrovascular/peripheral arterial disease, family history of AAA, hyperlipidaemia, hypertension, smoking.

queries.query: What imaging modality is recommended for diagnosis or surveillance of AAA?

answer_passages.why: Rec 7: ultrasonography recommended for first line diagnosis and surveillance of small AAA. Rec 9: CTA for treatment planning once threshold met and for diagnosis of rupture.
Ultrasound recommended, when feasible, as the preferred imaging modality for aneurysm screening and surveillance (1/A).
Offer an aortic ultrasound where asymptomatic AAA is being considered; report inner-to-inner maximum AP diameter.
Recommendations 13/14 specify imaging surveillance using ultrasound for small AAA.

queries.query: What factors influence the risk of AAA rupture?

answer_passages.why: Risk factors for AAA rupture include older age, female sex, smoking, and elevated blood pressure.

answer_passages.section_ref: 4.4 rupture risk vs diameter, sex, growth
answer_passages.why: Rupture risk by diameter (0.3-0.8%/yr below 55 mm in men); women have a fourfold greater rupture risk; rapid growth >10 mm/year associated with greater rupture risk.
With progressive aneurysm enlargement the risk of AAA rupture increases; quantified by diameter and time.
Annual rupture risk by diameter band in the UK screening programme; women had a fourfold greater rupture risk.

answer_passages.section_ref: 4.5 smoking and statins vs rupture risk
answer_passages.why: Rupture risk increased two-fold in current smokers; statins may reduce rupture risk.

queries.query: What are the recommendations for smoking cessation in patients with AAA?

answer_passages.why: Rec 16: all patients with AAA should receive cardiovascular risk factor management with smoking cessation. Rec 17: patients with a small AAA are recommended to stop smoking and receive help, to reduce growth rate and rupture risk (Class I, Level B).
Offer a referral to a stop smoking service to people with an AAA who smoke.
We recommend smoking cessation to reduce the risk of AAA growth and rupture (1/B).
We recommend smoking cessation for at least 2 weeks before aneurysm repair.

queries.query: What are the recommendations for women regarding AAA screening?

answer_passages.why: C recommendation: against routine screening in women who have never smoked and have no family history; I statement for women 65-75 who have ever smoked or have a family history.
Evidence insufficient for women 65-75 who ever smoked/family history; harms outweigh benefits for women who never smoked with no family history.
Limited evidence for screening in women, the only RCT underpowered; population screening in women has not been considered given lower prevalence.
Consider an aortic ultrasound for women aged 70 and over with listed risk factors if AAA not already excluded.
One-time ultrasound screening in men or women 65 to 75 years of age with a history of tobacco use.

queries.query: What are the differences between open surgical repair and EVAR recommendations?

answer_passages.why: Rec 65: EVAR preferred for most patients with suitable anatomy and reasonable life expectancy. Rec 66: open surgical repair preferred for most patients with long life expectancy. The surrounding text contrasts short-term survival benefit of EVAR against long-term durability.
Offer open surgical repair unless contraindicated; consider EVAR for abdominal copathology; consider EVAR or conservative management if OSR contraindicated.
If anatomically feasible, EVAR recommended over open repair for a ruptured AAA.
